Sanjay Patel: Quick sync — I'm drafting a short PRD/RFC for a runtime 'priority matrix' that ties kernel selection, attention opt heuristics, and KV cache policy to customer workload profiles. Want to nail scope + launch gates before I start the RFC.
Maria Chen: +1. Can you summarize the customer-driven asks we're trying to satisfy? helps prioritize.
Sanjay Patel: Two customer asks surfaced this week: (1) enterprise search team needs consistent p99 latency for short queries (<32 tokens) across peaks, (2) summarization partner needs higher throughput for long-context batches (8k+ tokens) with acceptable quality drop. Both want canary timelines.
Devin Park: So it's a tradeoff: optimize for low-latency kernels + aggressive KV prefetching for short seqs vs. memory-efficient kernels + relaxed prefetch/eviction to handle long seqs. We should capture tolerances (latency, cost, quality) as acceptance criteria.
Avery Li: Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- p99 latency (short path) <= 60ms per token for 95% of traffic during our test window
- end-to-end throughput for long-batch workload >= 2x current baseline or cost/token <= 0.8x
- quality regression: BLEU/ROUGE/paired-rank drop <= 1 percentage point vs baseline prompts
- fallback correctness: when fallback kernel triggers, completeness of output preserved (no truncated sequences)
Maria Chen: Edge cases to include in PRD:
- mixed requests (short + long) in same batch -> routing correctness
- streaming with kv-cache warmup latency spikes
- quantized kernel causing subtle tokenization differences
- request cancellation while KV fetch in-flight
Devin Park: We should add SLOs for fallback frequency: fallback to slower but compatible kernel should occur <0.5% of requests in steady state, and trigger alert when >1% in 10m window.
Sanjay Patel: Nice. For rollout plan I suggest: RFC -> dev prototype on canary cluster -> closed beta with enterprise search partner -> broad canary (5% traffic) -> 25% -> 100%. Each step has gating metrics.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: canary cluster deploy scheduled by @Sanjay for 2024-04-02T09:00Z. CI will block on perf/regression checks.
Avery Li: Minimal config snippet we can include in PRD for policy mapping:
```
priority_matrix:
  - profile: short_latency
    kernel_pref: fast-attn-low-latency
    kv_policy: aggressive-prefetch
    fallback: compatible-slow
  - profile: long_throughput
    kernel_pref: mem-efficient-attn
    kv_policy: lazy-load-evict-lru
    fallback: compatible-memstable
```
Devin Park: Tests to add to RFC: synthetic microbench (seq len sweep), mixed workload replay from prod trace, model-quality A/B with held-out prompts, interrupt/cancel scenario test.
Maria Chen: Who volunteers to own the draft RFC + PRD? I'll own the acceptance criteria section and edge cases. @Sanjay want you to own rollout plan and canary ops.
Sanjay Patel: I can take rollout + gating. @Devin take perf test harness and kernel eval matrix. @Avery can you document config + API changes for routing policies?
Avery Li: Yup, will do. I'll sketch the config API in the RFC and add examples.
OpsBot: note: test infra quota request approved for canary cluster: 4x p4d hours.
Sanjay Patel: Plan: I'll open RFC draft today, tag reviewers (Maria, Devin, Avery, infra). Target: RFC published by EOD tomorrow, 2-day review window, then prototype sprint next week. Any objections?
Maria Chen: No objections. :+1:
Devin Park: SGTM. One ask: include rollback criteria explicitly (latency/quality/cost thresholds).
Sanjay Patel: Agreed — will add rollback thresholds and alerting runbook.
Avery Li: I'll add config validation checks to prevent invalid policy combos.
Sanjay Patel: Great. I'll post the RFC link here when it's up.
